decision_matrix.use_when: The methodology choice changes a runtime boundary, public interface, data contract, release gate, or operating responsibility.
decision_matrix.avoid_when: Adjacent doctrine would only restate generic best practice without changing the next concrete action.
decision_matrix.implications: Retrieve the adjacent node once, then update specs, generated artifacts, tests, or release evidence as appropriate.

tradeoffs.option_a: Proceed quickly with a plausible delivery pattern.
tradeoffs.option_b: Pause to diagnose assumptions, users, constraints, and proof.
tradeoffs.guidance: Favor speed for reversible local work; favor diagnosis when the decision affects users, contracts, release safety, or long-lived architecture.

tradeoffs.option_a: Consider the full operating context before action.
tradeoffs.option_b: Select the smallest practice route that changes the next step.
tradeoffs.guidance: Start broad enough to protect intent, then narrow to one action, one artifact, and one proof surface.

tradeoffs.option_a: Rely on expert judgment when evidence is incomplete.
tradeoffs.option_b: Delay until stronger evidence is available.
tradeoffs.guidance: Proceed with named assumptions only when the proof plan can falsify them; otherwise surface the gap as a decision gate.

capture: Capture the user outcome, assumptions, constraints, selected practice route, rejected adjacent routes, and unresolved risks.
Capture the artifact that should change because this methodology was selected: plan, spec, test, runbook, memo, scaffold, or release note.
generate: Generate only artifacts that make the next step clearer: focused plans, acceptance criteria, proof checklists, operating runbooks, decision records, or scoped implementation tasks.
When the practice implies multiple workstreams, generate an ordered sequence with owners, dependencies, evidence gates, and explicit deferrals.
defer: Defer implementation choices that depend on unresolved user intent, material risk, data ownership, external systems, or release constraints.
Defer broad templates when a narrower methodology, architecture, interface, or spec node owns the concrete decision.
proof: Proof must demonstrate that the selected methodology changed action: clearer intent, safer sequencing, stronger acceptance criteria, or better validation evidence.
A later agent should be able to reconstruct the choice from specs, tests, generated artifacts, issue notes, or command output without relying on chat history.

intent: Record changed user outcomes, non-goals, assumptions, acceptance criteria, and clarification decisions introduced by methodology/EXECUTIVE_ALIGNMENT.
Preserve unresolved uncertainty instead of converting it into confident implementation scope.
architecture: Record changed boundaries, ownership, sequencing, deployment shape, or state assumptions when this practice affects system design.
Link any architectural decision back to the method, evidence, and tradeoff that made it necessary.
interfaces: Record new or changed commands, schemas, payloads, APIs, generated files, review contracts, or compatibility promises.
Do not imply a public interface from methodology alone; route to interface doctrine when compatibility is affected.
operations: Record owners, runbooks, monitoring expectations, rollout cadence, support paths, and escalation triggers when work affects operations.
Separate one-time project steps from durable operating responsibilities.
security: Record trust boundaries, sensitive data assumptions, abuse cases, access controls, and review gates when this methodology touches risk.
Treat unverified external input, generated content, and production-impacting changes as requiring explicit safety evidence.
validation: Record the proof plan, commands, fixtures, acceptance checks, and evidence threshold required before completion can be claimed.
Make failed, skipped, or environment-blocked proof visible rather than replacing it with narrative confidence.
semantics: Record terminology, decision criteria, metric definitions, ownership language, and behavior meanings that must stay stable across agents.
Update semantics when a methodology reframes what done, safe, accepted, or successful means.
proof: Proof should tie the selected practice to concrete repository state, executable checks, review evidence, or a named blocker.
Completion claims must state what was verified, what remains deferred, and which assumptions are still load-bearing.

static: The node is linked from core/METHODOLOGY or a narrower methodology parent and is reachable through relevant lookup terms.
Structured doctrine fields are present, non-empty, and preserve enough guidance for init, routing, scaffolding, specs, and proof planning.
runtime: A representative agent can retrieve the node and produce one sharper question, next action, artifact, or proof expectation.
When the methodology changes implementation or release behavior, tests or command output verify the affected path.
release: Generated specs or issue evidence are refreshed when methodology doctrine changes accepted scope, routes, or proof expectations.
Release evidence states any validation caveat, environmental blocker, or intentionally deferred risk.
